commands.name: alphero-deck
commands.description: Generate a minimal, branded Alphero HTML slide deck. Single self-contained file, light theme, Lexend font, arrow-key + on-screen navigation, fade transitions. Use when creating a demo, capability overview, or internal presentation in the Alphero style. (user)

commands.name: alphero-voice
commands.description: Rewrite an article so it reads as though it were published on Alphero Intelligence (alphero.com/intelligence), following the style guide derived from all 42 live articles. Use when asked to put a piece "in the Alphero voice", make a draft "sound like Alphero Intelligence", write a new post for the site, or refresh the guide against newly published articles. (user)

commands.name: architecture-audit
commands.description: Runs a fresh-eyes architectural audit of any repository, writes an architecture_roadmap.md of what to keep, refactor and add, then orchestrates the fixes through isolated sub-agents gated on deterministic checks. Use when the user wants an impartial review of a codebase's architecture, wants technical debt or "code slop" found and removed, asks whether the foundation is sound before building on it, wants dead code, redundant abstractions, missing boundaries or inconsistent patterns identified, or wants a large clean-up sequenced and delegated. Trigger it on phrasing like "take a step back and look at this codebase", "audit the architecture", "is this repo a mess", "de-slop this", "review this with fresh eyes", or "what should we fix before adding more features". (user)

commands.name: chiaroscuro
commands.description: Create distinctive, non-generic UI design direction, wireframes, Tailwind v4 visual systems, @theme tokens, and design specs, plus UI polish, dark mode, responsive adaptation, and live variant comparison. Use when asked to design a UI, establish a visual direction, produce a design spec, remove decorative UI furniture or system leakage, make a screen memorable, or clean up AI-looking Tailwind/React work. Assumes Tailwind v4. For reuse audits or shared-component extraction, use componentize. (user)

commands.name: componentize
commands.description: Audit a codebase for duplicated UI and repeated component patterns; identify, plan, or implement scoped shared components and UI package changes. Use when asked to componentize an app, reduce duplicated or repeated UI, adapt components with props/composition, create or use a Turborepo ui package, promote React/Tailwind reuse across apps/packages, or componentize a visually referenced region like "the panel on the right." For a standalone or publishable package, use aperture. (user)

commands.name: create-ui
commands.description: Turn a Figma frame into a reviewed implementation plan for building it in this repo. Use whenever the user mentions Figma or pastes any figma.com URL (figma.com/design/…, figma.com/file/…, a link containing ?node-id=), or asks to build, make, implement, code up or recreate a UI, component, page, screen, modal or layout from a Figma design, mockup, frame or link — including when they only ask about part of one, or supply the link alongside other instructions. A Figma link is sufficient on its own; use this before reading files or exploring the codebase. Extracts a token-mapped spec and reference render, resolves ambiguities with the user, and writes a plan a separate agent implements. (user)

commands.name: grok
commands.description: Quiz the user on a branch diff, commit, PR or feature until they understand it at a system level. First binary-searches what they already know with AskUserQuestion probes, then quizzes only the gaps — why decisions were made, what breaks without them, how the pieces interact. Use when asked to "quiz me", "test my understanding", "make sure I get this code", "grok" a change, or review what a branch/commit/feature does from the learner's side. (user)

commands.name: heathen
commands.description: No gods, no god files. Find and refactor god components, god scripts, oversized modules, tangled multi-responsibility files, and duplicated logic in JavaScript/TypeScript codebases. Use when asked to audit for large components or scripts, split files into meaningful pieces, simplify overgrown React components, or create a safe decomposition order with tests. Duplicated UI components belong in componentize; heathen targets logic, modules, scripts, and file decomposition. (user)

commands.name: human-writer
commands.description: Edit text to remove signs of AI-generated writing. Use when reviewing or revising prose to make it sound natural, specific, and human-written. Detects and rewrites AI vocabulary, significance inflation, promotional language, -ing padding, em dash overuse, rule-of-three, negative parallelisms, pseudo-profound flourishes, dying metaphors, vague attributions, filler phrases, sycophantic tone, extrapolation to universal principles, and formulaic structure. Triggers include "humanize this", "make this sound human", "remove AI patterns", "edit for voice", "deslop this", or any request to clean up AI-sounding text. (user)

commands.name: improve-claude-judge
commands.description: Review Claude Code session history and local Laya hook judgements, create evidence-backed LLM labels, and test and apply useful refinements to the local Claude Judge integration. Invoke on demand to assess whether the judge helps or discover better uses. (user)

commands.name: marginalia
commands.description: Add useful, concise JSDoc to JavaScript and TypeScript code, especially public package APIs, exported functions, classes, React components, hooks, complex types, and behavior where IDE hover help matters. Use when asked to add or improve JSDoc/code comments for public APIs, exported symbols, generated API docs, IDE hover help, or package publishing documentation without changing behavior. (user)

commands.name: penpot-design
commands.description: Agentic design work in Penpot through the Penpot MCP server. Bring a live page, local dev server, HTML or design file into Penpot; audit, tokenise and refine it into a coherent system with components; then implement approved boards in code by reading them live. Use whenever the user mentions Penpot, wants a page or URL turned into editable design layers, asks to polish, systematise, tokenise or make a design coherent in a design tool, wants components or variants built, or asks to implement a Penpot board, component or selection. (user)

commands.name: poc-to-mvp
commands.description: Turn a working agentic proof-of-concept into a fast, cheap, mostly-deterministic production MVP. Inventories every LLM/agent call site, works out which ones a plain system does better, measures a baseline, plans the migration in shippable phases, then executes it behind seams that let you swap implementations. Use this whenever someone has a working AI prototype and wants to productionise, harden, speed up, or cut the cost of it — including when they say a pipeline is too slow or too expensive, ask which steps really need a model, want to replace agents or LLM calls with deterministic code, want to move retrieval or ranking out of an agent and into embeddings, scoring and code, want to introduce caching, small models or build-time precomputation, or want to know where to put abstractions before scaling. Also use when a prompt has quietly grown into a specification full of rules, when someone is about to fix a systematic pipeline failure by adding another sentence to a prompt, when an agentic loop is doing work whose control flow is actually fixed, or when an LLM is composing or laying out an answer that could be assembled from approved components instead. Covers giving editors and non-engineers a real control surface over relevance and ranking, which an agent cannot offer. (user)

commands.name: polish
commands.description: Review work-in-progress code, complete missing logic, fix bugs, and refactor to match project standards. (user)
commands.argumentHint: path or glob,optional — defaults to uncommitted changes

commands.name: prototype-to-production
commands.description: Orchestrates hardening a prototype codebase into a production-grade system by planning job-shaped modules, delegating them to isolated sub-agents, and gating every result behind deterministic checks. Use this whenever the user asks to make a codebase production-ready, harden or productionise a prototype, do a large multi-module refactor, add error handling/validation/type safety/test coverage across a repo, or asks how to break a big codebase job into parallel sub-agents. Trigger it even when the user only says something like "this is a demo, clean it up properly" or "get this repo ready to ship" without using the word "production". (user)

commands.name: unslop
commands.description: Strip the tells of machine-written code from a diff without changing what it does - comments narrating the line below, one-caller wrappers, guards against states the types forbid, options nobody passes, decorative log output and leftover scaffolding. Run it before commit or review. Behaviour-changing cleanups belong elsewhere - fallbacks and swallowed errors are `fail-fast`, oversized modules are `heathen`, doc comments worth keeping are `marginalia`, and prose is `deslop`. (user)

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:a11y-debugging
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Uses Chrome DevTools MCP for accessibility (a11y) debugging and auditing based on web.dev guidelines. Use when testing semantic HTML, ARIA labels, focus states, keyboard navigation, tap targets, and color contrast.

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:chrome-devtools
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Uses Chrome DevTools via MCP for efficient debugging, troubleshooting and browser automation. Use when debugging web pages, automating browser interactions, analyzing performance, or inspecting network requests. This skill does not apply to `--slim` mode (MCP configuration).

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:chrome-devtools-cli
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Use this skill to write shell scripts or run shell commands to automate tasks in the browser or otherwise use Chrome DevTools via CLI.

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:cookie-debugging
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Uses Chrome DevTools MCP for inspecting, debugging, and testing cookies, session state, authentication issues, and cookie consent compliance. Use when diagnosing 401/403 errors, authentication redirects, session expiration, Cookie/Set-Cookie header issues, cookie banner consent conformance, or third-party cookie/SameSite/Partitioned cookie warnings.

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:debug-optimize-lcp
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Guides debugging and optimizing Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) using Chrome DevTools MCP tools. Use this skill whenever the user asks about LCP performance, slow page loads, Core Web Vitals optimization, or wants to understand why their page's main content takes too long to appear. Also use when the user mentions "largest contentful paint", "page load speed", "CWV", or wants to improve how fast their hero image or main content renders.

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:memory-leak-debugging
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Diagnoses and resolves memory leaks in JavaScript/Node.js applications. Use when a user reports high memory usage, OOM errors, or wants to capture, compare, or inspect heap snapshots with Chrome DevTools MCP memory tools.

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:troubleshooting
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Uses Chrome DevTools MCP and documentation to troubleshoot connection and target issues. Trigger this skill when list_pages, new_page, or navigate_page fail, or when the server initialization fails.

commands.name: alphero-cloud:express-ts-bff
commands.description: (alphero-cloud) Migrates or bootstraps an Express BFF to TypeScript with a typed route-builder (Zod + authz), Zod env schema validation, Helmet CSP/HSTS, and CI typecheck/lint/test gates. Use when the user asks to apply the TypeScript Express BFF procedure, add a route-builder, harden Helmet/CSP, or port a Node server to this stack.

commands.name: alphero-shared:agent-setup
commands.description: (alphero-shared) Set up or audit Claude Code agentic development in an existing repository — CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/, .claude/settings.json, permissions and deterministic lifecycle hooks. Use when the user wants to set up the agent environment, onboard a repo to Claude Code, configure hooks or settings.json, write or trim a CLAUDE.md, stop Claude repeating the same mistakes in a codebase, enforce project rules programmatically rather than by instruction, or cut the token cost of working in a repo. Also use for "make Claude reliable in this repo", "add guardrails", "why does Claude keep doing X here", and reviewing an existing .claude/ directory.

commands.name: alphero-shared:commit-crafter
commands.description: (alphero-shared) Use when asked to write, generate, reword or format a git commit message — from staged changes, a pasted diff, or a bare "what should I call this commit". Produces a Conventional Commits message (type, optional scope, imperative subject under 50 characters, optional body wrapped at 72) and hands it back in a code block to copy. It writes the message only; committing stays with the user.

commands.name: alphero-shared:contribute-skill
commands.description: (alphero-shared) Use when asked to add, contribute, share, publish, upstream or PR an existing skill to the Alphero skills repo (alphero-ai-skills, "the team skills", "the shared skills repo"). Reviews the skill for repo-specific content, client information and team value, saves a revised copy without touching the original, picks the discipline plugin, and opens a PR against main — or walks the user through doing it by hand when they lack access.
commands.argumentHint: path to the skill directory or its SKILL.md

commands.name: alphero-shared:readme-maintainer
commands.description: (alphero-shared) Use this skill when asked to update, sync, or regenerate the root README.md of the alphero-ai-skills repository after adding, moving, renaming, or removing a skill or plugin.

commands.name: alphero-web:add-tsdoc
commands.description: (alphero-web) Use when the user asks to add, fill in, or update TSDoc on one or more existing React components that are undocumented or only partially documented. Takes one or more component file paths as arguments. Adds a one-line inline TSDoc comment on each undocumented prop field, and a short TSDoc block above the component itself with a single `@example` that exercises every prop.

commands.name: alphero-web:fullstack-typescript-architecture
commands.description: (alphero-web) Use when starting, scaffolding, extending or reviewing a full-stack TypeScript monorepo on the house reference stack — React with TanStack Router and TanStack Query, Express, Zod contracts shared between them, Vitest and MSW, Vite, pnpm workspaces. Also use when asked what the agreed package structure, dependency rules, auth flow or security guardrails are for one, or whether a change matches them. Routes to the reference documentation; read the relevant section before proposing a structure, a package boundary or an alternative library.

commands.name: alphero-web:tomopai-check
commands.description: (alphero-web) Use when asked whether a web component, page, route, PR or whole site meets Tomopai (Alphero's accessibility baseline), to run a Tomopai / accessibility / a11y check or audit, to fill in the Web column of a project's Tomopai spreadsheet, or to check WCAG basics before design or QA handoff. Works in any React, TanStack, Next, Vue, Svelte or plain HTML repo with no setup. Runs deterministic checks against every row of the Alphero Tomopai Checklist 2026 — a dependency-free static scan of TSX/JSX/Vue/HTML/CSS, a live Playwright + axe-core scan of URLs (44px targets, tab order and focus visibility, 200% text, six viewports, reduced motion, colour-blindness screenshots, optional site crawl) and a design-token contrast calculator — then reports PASS / FAIL / MANUAL per row with file:line fixes, the suggested spreadsheet status, and exactly what a human still has to test.
commands.argumentHint: [component file, directory, URL — or nothing to be asked]

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (living docs people share, comment on and edit; use only when the user asks for one: names a doc, document, page, memo, spec, PRD, runbook or write-up, asks for somewhere to share or keep editing something, or says yes to your doc offer; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat (at most a one-line doc offer); a report, status update, recap or "something I can send them" with no form named → ask first: reply, doc or file?; tabs hold tables and live charts too; a pasted claude.ai/code/artifact/… link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; not HTML pages, apps or plain chat answers; a .docx/.pptx/.xlsx/PDF asked for by name → that format's skill): asked for one → no docs-connector instructions in context? call the docs connector's `guide` with topic.instructions first, then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. Documenting code means docstrings or repo docs, not a doc. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

agents.name: build

agents.name: claude
agents.description: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed.

agents.name: codebase-search
agents.description: Locates code across the repo. Use proactively for "where is X", "what uses Y", finding all call sites.

agents.name: Explore
agents.description: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions.

agents.name: general-purpose
agents.description: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you.

agents.name: penpot-implementer
agents.description: Coding agent for the end of the Penpot design workflow. Implements an approved Penpot board, component or selection in the current repo by reading it live through the Penpot MCP, mapping every value onto the repo's tokens, and verifying the build against a board export. Use when a design refined in Penpot is ready to build.

agents.name: Plan
agents.description: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs.

agents.name: research

agents.name: review
agents.description: Reviews what the build room produced. Use last, to check the output against the request.
